name: Arize Phoenix
pros: Self-hosting is genuinely free, with no per-trace bill at scale
OpenTelemetry and OpenInference native, so instrumentation is portable rather than vendor-specific
Retrieval and embedding analysis are deeper than most general-purpose tracers
Runs locally in a notebook for development, which shortens the loop
files: Datasets and experiments as first-class objects; embeddings analysis for retrieval pipelines.
value: The source-available observability platform from Arize, built on OpenTelemetry with OpenInference semantic conventions for LLM spans. It runs in a notebook, on a laptop, or as a container in your own cloud, and covers tracing, datasets, LLM-as-judge evaluation, RAG-specific retrieval metrics, and embedding drift visualisation. Its distinguishing property is that instrumentation is standard: the same OpenTelemetry spans can be routed to Phoenix today and a different backend tomorrow without re-instrumenting the application.
engine: Self-hosted or Phoenix Cloud. OpenTelemetry collector ingesting OpenInference-shaped spans.
latency: Asynchronous span export; no proxy in the request path.

pricing.includes: Full tracing, evals, datasets, embeddings analysis under Elastic License 2.0

pricing.limits: Commercial tiers meter on spans per month, which climbs quickly for agents that emit thousands of spans per run

quality: Strongest of the open options for retrieval-heavy work, with embedding drift and RAG metrics that generic tracers lack. Prompt-and-notebook centric heritage means very long agent runs can be laborious to read as a raw span tree.
tagline: Self-hostable LLM tracing and evaluation built on open standards, so your trace data stays yours and stays portable.
use_cases: Debugging RAG pipelines where the failure is in retrieval rather than generation
Keeping prompts and completions inside your own infrastructure for data-residency reasons
Instrumenting once with OpenTelemetry and staying free to change backends
Comparing evaluation runs across prompt or model changes
governance_note: Self-hosting resolves the question that dominates observability procurement: prompts and completions never leave your environment, so trace capture does not become a new data-transfer decision to justify. The remaining obligations move to you rather than disappearing, since retention, access control, and encryption of the trace store are now your responsibility, and a trace store holds exactly the sensitive text a data map has to account for. The OpenTelemetry foundation is itself a governance asset: instrumentation that is not vendor-specific means an observability vendor changing hands, raising prices, or entering maintenance mode does not force a re-instrumentation project.
training_optout: Self-hosted deployments send nothing to the vendor. Hosted tiers are governed by the Arize agreement; verify current terms.
